main_text.l: orius est, officiosumque sermonem, nil esse præter marsupium palpantes blanditias, & sub composita larva inhiantem lucro cupidine: Quin fuerunt, qui improbo spiritu fanatici, lividum calamum listrinxêre in Dithyrambū: & laudibus, quibus nos gentilis alicujus pietas irradiaverat, diras opposuerunt: Adeò tenebriones istos exagitat, quod se non celat decus. Expedit ergo quam suos laudare, cum suis laudanda facere: & Exteros tacito illo ac suavi filo obsequentes, in venerationem Patriæ pertrahere, quàm intempestivo laudum crepitaculo, quasi vis inferretur, obluctantes experiri.

page.notes: The first word is a fragment: its initial letter is cut off by the gutter, so it is given as "orius". The line "sermo-/nem" and "obse-/quentes" are hyphenated at line ends in print. The faint text below the main text is show-through from the other side and is not transcribed.
